Forecast Discussion

The Nor’easter that has been plaguing the Mid-Atlantic and coastal New England is spinning down/weakening. Meanwhile, broad high pressure extends in an arc from Lake Superior into Illinois and spreads into the Deep South.

This high pressure system will continue to moderate under the strong late-September sun angle, promoting fair weather and a slow but steady warming trend. By Thursday and Friday, high temperatures will be running more than 10-degrees above normal.

Next up will be a cold front, scheduled to arrive here Friday evening or night. The front stalls to our south over the weekend, with potential low-pressure waves riding along it during Saturday and Sunday. This will represent our next chance for rainfall for the High Country and Southwest Virginia, as the warmer weather is replaced by cooler air to the north of the frontal boundary.
